SIKA MONOTOP®-612 N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika MonoTop®-612 N, April 2023, Version 01.05 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sika-monotop-612n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika MonoTop®-612 N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.05).
1.2 Product description. Sika® MonoTop-612 N is a cement-based, one component low permeability concrete repair mortar, containing silica fume and polymer, meeting the requirements of Class R4 of EN 1504-3.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - ▪ For repairing high strength concrete >45MPa
    - ▪ High Build repairs horizontal, vertical and overhead ▪ For exterior and interior use
    - ▪ New and old concrete repairs
    - ▪ Marine repairs
    - ▪ Trafficable repair applications
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika MonoTop®-612 N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: POLYMER MODIFIED HIGH STRENGTH, HIGH BUILD CONCRETE REPAIR MORTAR
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - AS 4020:2018 potable water approved
    - Qld Roads (TMR) Section 5. Registered and Conforming Products. Part 5.34 Repair Mortars
    - RTA Rapid Mortar Bar Test RTA T363 - Alkali Reactive Particles <0.10% (Non-Reactive).
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-3: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Description (p.1).
    - AS 4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - AS 1012.17: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - ASTM C 348: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength in flexure (p.2).
    - AS 1012.10: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Splitting tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - AS 2350.13: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shrinkage (p.2).
    - EN 12617-4: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Restrained shrinkage / expansion (p.2).
    - ASTM C 1585: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Capillary absorption (p.2).
    - EN 1504: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: System Information > System structure (p.2).
    - AS 2350.4: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Final set time (p.3); Application Information > Initial set time (p.3).
    - EN 1504-10: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Important Considerations (p.3).
    - EN1504-10: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Reinforcement: (p.3).
    - ISO 8501-1: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Reinforcement: (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Compatible with Sika® FerroGard® corrosion
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer - inhibitors.
    - Compatible with Sika® FerroGard® Sacrificial
2.6 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer - Anode System.
    - High build up to 100mm in one application*
    - Low shrinkage
    - High workability
    - Very high resistivity mortar for durable new work concrete repairs
    - AS/AZS 4020:2018 Approved for Potable/ drinking water contact
    - Sulphate resistant in marine
2.7 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Portland cement, polymer redispersable powder, selected aggregates and additives
    - Appearance and colour: Grey powder
    - Density: Fresh mortar density ~2.20 kg/l
2.8 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Maximum grain size: Dmax: 2.0 mm
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~ 25 GPa @ 28 days (AS 1012.17)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 2.0 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Restrained shrinkage / expansion: ≥ 2.0 MPa @ 28 days (EN 12617-4)
    - Capillary absorption: 3.2 x 10⁻⁴(mm/√s) (ASTM C 1585)
    - Chloride ion diffusion resistance: 1.15 E-12 (m2/s) (NT443)
2.9 Compressive strength.
    | 1 day | ~ 18 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 50 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 70 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
    Note printed: Material and curing conditions at 23 oC / 50% r.h Above results based on 50mm x 50mm cubes @ 2.8 litres water per 20kg bag
2.10 Tensile strength in flexure.
    | 1 day | ~ 4 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 8 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 9 MPa |
    Test method printed: (ASTM C 348)
2.11 Splitting tensile strength.
    | 28 days | ~ 5.0 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1012.10)
2.12 Shrinkage.
    | 7 days | ~ 250 microstrains |
    | 28 days | ~ 650 microstrains |
    Test method printed: (AS 2350.13)
2.13 Electrical resistivity.
    | 7 days | ~ 33,000 Ω.cm |
    | 28 days | ~ 139,000 Ω.cm |
    | 56 days | ~ 171,000 Ω.cm |
    | 90 days | ~ 211,000 Ω.cm |
    Test method printed: (FM5-578)
    Note printed: 50mm Probe Spacing
2.14 System structure. Sika MonoTop®-612 N is part of the range of Sika mortars complying with the relevant part of European Standard EN 1504 and comprising of: Bonding Primer / Reinforcement; Corrosion Protection
    | Sika Monotop® - 910 N | Normal Use |
    | SikaTop® Armatec® 110 Epocem® | Demanding requirements |
    | Repair Mortar |
    | Sika Monotop® - 612 N | Class R4 concrete repair hand and |
    | machine applied |
    | Levelling Mortar |
    | Sika Monotop® - 723 N | Normal Use |
    | Sikagard® - 720 Epocem® | Demanding requirements |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.15 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20 kg bag
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of manufacture
    - Storage conditions: Product must be stored in dry controlled conditions

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.05) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Concrete. The concrete shall be thoroughly clean, free from dust, loose material, surface contamination and materials which reduce bond or prevent suction or wetting by repair materials. Delaminated, weak, damaged and deteriorated concrete and where necessary sound concrete shall be removed by suitable means.
3.3 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Steel Reinforcement. Rust, scale, mortar, concrete, dust and other loose and deleterious material which reduces bond or contributes to corrosion shall be removed. Surfaces shall be prepared using abrasive blast cleaning techniques or high pressure water-blasting to Sa 2 (ISO 8501-1) Reference shall be made to EN1504-10 for specific requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.05) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: 2.8 to 3.0 litres of water for 20 kg powder
    - Consumption: This depends on the substrate roughness and thickness of layer applied. As a guide, ~ 19.0 kg of powder per cm thick per m2
    - Yield: 20 kg of powder yields approximately 10.9 litres of mortar
    - Layer thickness: min. 5 mm / max. 100 mm
    - Pot Life: ~ 35 minutes at +23°C
    - Initial set time: ~ 2.0 hours (AS 2350.4)
    - Final set time: ~ 5.0 hours (AS 2350.4)
4.3 Mixing. Sika MonoTop®-612 N can be mixed with a low speed (< 500 rpm) hand drill mixer or for machine application, using a force action mixer 2 to 3 bags or more at once depending the type and size of mixer. In small quantity, Sika MonoTop®-612 N can also be manually mixed. Pour the recommended water in a suitable mixing container. While stirring slowly, add the powder to the water and mix thoroughly at least for 3 minutes to the required consistency.
4.4 Application - Bonding Primer. On a well prepared and roughened substrate a bonding primer is generally not required for this product. When a bonding primer is required, refer to the System Information above for compatible Sika products and refer to the relevant Product Data Sheet for instructions. All small amount of Sika MonoTop®-612 N can also be mixed slightly wetter than normal and used as a scratch coat to promote adhesion of the repair mortar to the substrate. Any bonding primer shall be applied on a pre-wet substrate in saturated surface dry (SSD) condition and subsequent application of the repair mortar shall be applied wet on wet with the bonding primer.
4.5 Application - Reinforcement Corrosion Protection.
    - Where a reinforcement coating is required the application of a repair mortar shall be applied wet on dry with the reinforcement corrosion protection. Refer to the System Information above for compatible Sika products and refer to the relevant Product Data Sheet for more detailed information about the reinforcement corrosion product. Sika MonoTop®-612 N can be applied either manually using traditional techniques or mechanically using wet spray equipment. Thoroughly pre-wet the prepared substrate a recommended 2 hours before application. Keep the surface wet and maintain in SSD condition. The surface shall appear a dark matt appearance without glistening and surface pores and pits shall not contain water.
    - When manually applying first make a scratch coat by firmly scrapping the repair mortar over the substrate surface to form a thin layer and fill any pores or pits in the surface. Ensure the whole surface to be repaired is covered by the scratch coat. Build up layers from bottom to top by pressing mortar well into the repair area. The surface can be finished according to the requirements using a float while wet or with a relevant rough-cast tool as soon as the mortar has started to stiffen.
4.6 Curing treatment. Protect the fresh mortar immediately from premature drying using an appropriate curing method e.g. curing compound, moist geotextile membrane, polythene sheet etc.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened material can only be mechanically removed.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Refer to the Method Statement for Concrete Repair using Sika MonoTop® system for more information regarding substrate preparation or refer to the recommendations provided in EN 1504-10
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind.
    - Do not add water over recommended dosage.
    - Apply only to sound, prepared substrate.
    - Do not add additional water during the surface finishing as this will cause discolouration and cracking.
    - Protect freshly applied material from freezing.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C minimum; +30 °C maximum
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C minimum; +30 °C maximum
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind.
    - Protect freshly applied material from freezing.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: 1 day | ~ 18 MPa; 7 days | ~ 50 MPa; 28 days | ~ 70 MPa (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~ 25 GPa @ 28 days (AS 1012.17)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: 1 day | ~ 4 MPa; 7 days | ~ 8 MPa; 28 days | ~ 9 MPa (ASTM C 348)
    - Splitting tensile strength: 28 days | ~ 5.0 MPa (AS 1012.10)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 2.0 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Shrinkage: 7 days | ~ 250 microstrains; 28 days | ~ 650 microstrains (AS 2350.13)
    - Restrained shrinkage / expansion: ≥ 2.0 MPa @ 28 days (EN 12617-4)
    - Electrical resistivity: 7 days | ~ 33,000 Ω.cm; 28 days | ~ 139,000 Ω.cm; 56 days | ~ 171,000 Ω.cm; 90 days | ~ 211,000 Ω.cm (FM5-578)
    - Capillary absorption: 3.2 x 10⁻⁴(mm/√s) (ASTM C 1585)
    - Chloride ion diffusion resistance: 1.15 E-12 (m2/s) (NT443)
    - Initial set time: ~ 2.0 hours (AS 2350.4)
    - Final set time: ~ 5.0 hours (AS 2350.4)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika MonoTop®-612 N, April 2023, Version 01.05, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sika-monotop-612n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika MonoTop®-612 N, version 13/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sds-sika-monotop-612n.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
